1	# ADR-0094: Per-worktree virtual environments are declined; the packages are imported from source instead
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-08-22
5	- **Areas:** tooling, testing
6	- **Reversibility:** high
7	- **Decision-makers:** repository maintainers
8	- **Supersedes:** none
9	- **Supersedes in part:** none
10	- **Superseded by:** none
11	- **Superseded in part:** none
12	- **Related:** ADR-0036
13	
14	## Decision summary
15	
16	- **Decision:** We will not create a per-worktree virtual environment; `agentbundle` and `credbroker` are imported from source in this repository's own gates and tests.
17	- **Because:** the write a venv was meant to isolate no longer happens — no repository gate installs either package.
18	- **Applies to:** this repository's local development and test invocations. Adopter installs and CI runner provisioning are untouched.
19	- **Tradeoff accepted:** each new worktree still shares one interpreter's `site-packages`, so a distribution version skew there remains observable — `importlib.metadata.version()` can disagree with the imported module.
20	- **Revisit if:** a repository gate ever genuinely requires an installed (not merely importable) `agentbundle` or `credbroker`, or a supported sandbox gains the ability to run `pip install` without leaving unremovable litter.
21	
22	## Context
23	
24	Nine worktrees of this repository share one interpreter. A per-worktree virtual
25	environment was proposed to stop `pip install -e` from mutating that shared
26	environment — a real hazard, because an editable install is global to the
27	interpreter and one worktree's bootstrap can disturb another's running gates.
28	
29	Three facts, measured on 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-22, changed the picture.
30	
31	**The install was never required.** `Makefile:7` already places both package
32	directories on `PYTHONPATH` for every `make` target, and every invocation is
33	`$(PYTHON) -m agentbundle`, never the console script. The only thing missing was
34	a bare `pytest`, which has neither the working directory nor a `PYTHONPATH` of
35	its own; declaring `pythonpath` in `pyproject.toml` closes that. After that, no
36	repository gate installs either package, so a virtual environment would isolate
37	a write that no longer occurs.
38	
39	**A supervised worker cannot create a usable virtual environment at all.**
40	`python3 -m venv` fails inside `ensurepip` under the supervised worker's sandbox
41	— inside the workspace, in the system temporary directory, and with `TMPDIR`
42	redirected into the workspace. `python3 -m venv --without-pip` succeeds, so
43	directory creation is not the constraint.
44	
45	**The root cause is a sandbox policy denial, not configuration.** pip's `install`
46	unconditionally builds a network session (`get_default_session` →
47	`_create_truststore_ssl_context`) even under `--no-index`. That materialises
48	certifi's CA bundle as a temporary file carrying the macOS
49	`com.apple.provenance` extended attribute, and the sandbox denies both read and
50	unlink on it: `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. `EPERM`, not
51	`EACCES` — a policy refusal rather than a file mode. So no network allowlist,
52	path change, or permission grant helps.
53	
54	State the frame, because it is what localises the cause: those venv measurements
55	were taken under the supervised worker's sandbox. `python3 -m venv` succeeds
56	under an interactive session's sandbox on the same machine and the same
57	interpreter. The failure belongs to that sandbox's policy, not to the host or
58	the Python installation.
59	
60	## Decision
61	
62	**We will not introduce a per-worktree virtual environment**, and this
63	repository's gates and tests will import `agentbundle` and `credbroker` from
64	source.
65	
66	- **D1:** This repository introduces no per-worktree virtual environment.
67	- **D2:** This repository's own gates and tests import `agentbundle` and
68	  `credbroker` from source, not from an installed distribution.
69	- **D3:** Source resolution has exactly two mechanisms and no third —
70	  `PYTHONPATH` for `make` targets and `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath` for
71	  a bare `pytest` — and neither installs anything.
72	- **D4:** The decision governs this repository's own invocations only; adopter
73	  installs and CI runner provisioning are untouched, and an installed copy on a
74	  maintainer's machine stays legitimate.
75	
76	Source resolution has two mechanisms and no third: `PYTHONPATH` for `make`
77	targets (`Makefile:7`), and `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath` for a bare
78	`pytest`. Neither installs anything.
79	
80	The boundary is deliberate and narrow. This decision governs *this repository's
81	own* invocations. It says nothing about adopters, who install the package

87	use.

92	  change, no.

94	  worker cannot create a virtual environment with pip at all.

106	worker can run `pytest <path>` — the only form it can issue, with no environment
107	prefix — and get this worktree's source. Nothing must be provisioned before the
108	gates run beyond the genuine tooling (`ruff`, `mypy`, `pytest`, and the

124	would therefore never be recognised as in use unless the cleaner happened to be

# ADR-0094: Per-worktree virtual environments are declined; the packages are imported from source instead

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Areas:** tooling, testing
- **Reversibility:** high
- **Decision-makers:** repository maintainers
- **Supersedes:** none
- **Supersedes in part:** none
- **Superseded by:** none
- **Superseded in part:** none
- **Related:** ADR-0036

## Decision summary

- **Decision:** We will not create a per-worktree virtual environment; `agentbundle` and `credbroker` are imported from source in this repository's own gates and tests.
- **Because:** the write a venv was meant to isolate no longer happens — no repository gate installs either package.
- **Applies to:** this repository's local development and test invocations. Adopter installs and CI runner provisioning are untouched.
- **Tradeoff accepted:** each new worktree still shares one interpreter's `site-packages`, so a distribution version skew there remains observable — `importlib.metadata.version()` can disagree with the imported module.
- **Revisit if:** a repository gate ever genuinely requires an installed (not merely importable) `agentbundle` or `credbroker`, or a supported sandbox gains the ability to run `pip install` without leaving unremovable litter.

## Context

Nine worktrees of this repository share one interpreter. A per-worktree virtual
environment was proposed to stop `pip install -e` from mutating that shared
environment — a real hazard, because an editable install is global to the
interpreter and one worktree's bootstrap can disturb another's running gates.

Three facts, measured on 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-22, changed the picture.

**The install was never required.** `Makefile:7` already places both package
directories on `PYTHONPATH` for every `make` target, and every invocation is
`$(PYTHON) -m agentbundle`, never the console script. The only thing missing was
a bare `pytest`, which has neither the working directory nor a `PYTHONPATH` of
its own; declaring `pythonpath` in `pyproject.toml` closes that. After that, no
repository gate installs either package, so a virtual environment would isolate
a write that no longer occurs.

**A supervised worker cannot create a usable virtual environment at all.**
`python3 -m venv` fails inside `ensurepip` under the supervised worker's sandbox
— inside the workspace, in the system temporary directory, and with `TMPDIR`
redirected into the workspace. `python3 -m venv --without-pip` succeeds, so
directory creation is not the constraint.

**The root cause is a sandbox policy denial, not configuration.** pip's `install`
unconditionally builds a network session (`get_default_session` →
`_create_truststore_ssl_context`) even under `--no-index`. That materialises
certifi's CA bundle as a temporary file carrying the macOS
`com.apple.provenance` extended attribute, and the sandbox denies both read and
unlink on it: `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. `EPERM`, not
`EACCES` — a policy refusal rather than a file mode. So no network allowlist,
path change, or permission grant helps.

State the frame, because it is what localises the cause: those venv measurements
were taken under the supervised worker's sandbox. `python3 -m venv` succeeds
under an interactive session's sandbox on the same machine and the same
interpreter. The failure belongs to that sandbox's policy, not to the host or
the Python installation.

## Decision

**We will not introduce a per-worktree virtual environment**, and this
repository's gates and tests will import `agentbundle` and `credbroker` from
source.

- **D1:** This repository introduces no per-worktree virtual environment.
- **D2:** This repository's own gates and tests import `agentbundle` and
  `credbroker` from source, not from an installed distribution.
- **D3:** Source resolution has exactly two mechanisms and no third —
  `PYTHONPATH` for `make` targets and `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath` for
  a bare `pytest` — and neither installs anything.
- **D4:** The decision governs this repository's own invocations only; adopter
  installs and CI runner provisioning are untouched, and an installed copy on a
  maintainer's machine stays legitimate.

Source resolution has two mechanisms and no third: `PYTHONPATH` for `make`
targets (`Makefile:7`), and `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath` for a bare
`pytest`. Neither installs anything.

The boundary is deliberate and narrow. This decision governs *this repository's
own* invocations. It says nothing about adopters, who install the package
normally, and nothing about CI, where each job provisions a fresh runner on
which nothing is on `PYTHONPATH` and an install is the correct move. An
installed copy on a maintainer's machine remains entirely legitimate — it is how
the `agentbundle` console script exists, and an editable install is ADR-0036's
layer-3 catalogue-source detection mechanism. It is simply not what these gates
use.

## Decision drivers

- **Does the isolation protect a write that still happens?** After the source-import
  change, no.
- **Can every supported agent runtime execute the mechanism?** No — the supervised
  worker cannot create a virtual environment with pip at all.
- **Does the mechanism leave the shared environment worse than it found it?** Yes:
  each failed attempt leaves roughly 265KB of temporary files that the worker
  itself cannot delete, because the same policy that blocks reading them blocks
  unlinking them.
- **Does existing tooling already assume the mechanism is absent?** Yes — see the
  latent trap below.

## Consequences

so one worktree's setup cannot disturb another's running tests. A supervised
worker can run `pytest <path>` — the only form it can issue, with no environment
prefix — and get this worktree's source. Nothing must be provisioned before the
gates run beyond the genuine tooling (`ruff`, `mypy`, `pytest`, and the
requirements files named in the `Makefile`).

**Negative, accepted.** All worktrees continue to share one `site-packages`. When
the worktree source version leads the installed distribution — the normal state
during development — `importlib.metadata.version()` and the imported module
report different versions, and code that consults the former sees the older one.
That is a consequence to know about, not a defect to fix: both values are
legitimate, and the repository's own gates resolve the module from source.

**A latent trap this decision also avoids.** `tools/repo/worktree_hygiene.py`
lists `.venv`, `venv`, and `env` as deletable `dependencies` candidates
(`:63-65`). That is correct and stays. But its in-use guard resolves
distributions from `importlib.metadata.distributions()` on **the interpreter
running the cleaner** (`_installed_distribution_locations`, `:862-870`, consumed
by `_is_in_use` at `:1161` and at `:1736`). A per-worktree virtual environment
would therefore never be recognised as in use unless the cleaner happened to be
running from inside it — so the cleanup tool could delete a live environment out
from under a peer worktree. Introducing virtual environments would require
fixing that guard first. Not introducing them leaves nothing to fix.

**Revisit if:** a repository gate ever genuinely requires an installed rather
than importable `agentbundle` or `credbroker`, or a supported sandbox gains the
ability to run `pip install` without leaving unremovable litter.

## Confirmation

- **Mode:** lint/CI
- **Signal:** `make lint-editable-install` (`tools/repo/editable_install_guard.py`)
  fails when an editable install of either package points at a worktree other
  than the one being worked in — the state in which this decision has already
  been violated by someone. `test-unleased` depends on it, so the gates cannot
  pass in that state.
- **Owner:** repository maintainers
- **Residual:** the guard describes installs; it cannot prevent one being made.

  are both deliberately allowed, so a maintainer can still reach the harm state
  transiently by re-pointing an editable install while a peer's gates run. And
  nothing prevents creating a `.venv` by hand — the decision governs what the
  repository *requires*, not what a machine contains;
  `tools/repo/worktree_hygiene.py` would treat such a directory as a deletable
  dependency candidate, which is the trap the Consequences describe.

## Alternatives considered

**Per-worktree `.venv` (rejected).** Isolates a write that no longer happens;
cannot be created by the supervised worker at all; and would expose the
`_is_in_use` trap above. Rejected against all four decision drivers.

**Uninstall the global `agentbundle` and `credbroker` (rejected).** The
maintainer's installed copy is deliberate and is a real consumer surface — the
console script and ADR-0036's editable detection both depend on it. Removing it
to make tests tidier would break a legitimate workflow to fix a problem that
source imports already solve.

**One shared virtual environment for all worktrees (rejected).** Reintroduces
exactly the shared mutable state the proposal set out to eliminate, and still
cannot be created by the supervised worker.

**Do nothing (rejected).** Leaves a bare `pytest` importing whatever is
installed, and leaves the `Makefile` instructing each new session to write to
the shared environment — the write that caused the original hazard.

## References

- `tools/repo/build_gate_chain.py:70-82` — records that both packages are
  importable from source, so neither needs `pip install -e`.

13	
14	## Decision summary
15	
16	- **Decision:** Workflows detect eligible knowledge surfaces by capability;
17	  directly governed repository authorities remain directly readable, while an
18	  OKF-backed surface is accessed only through its explicitly invoked provider.
19	- **Because:** Domain grounding should use available knowledge without coupling a
20	  consumer to another pack's identity, installation layout, or raw corpus.
21	- **Applies to:** Portable workflows that perform domain grounding and packs
22	  that expose OKF-backed knowledge to same-pack or independent consumers.
23	- **Tradeoff accepted:** Provider owners must publish and verify a discoverable
24	  capability, while consumers must handle ambiguity, conflict, and absence.
25	- **Revisit if:** portable skill runtimes adopt a standard, security-preserving
26	  provider-capability negotiation protocol that subsumes this contract.
27	
28	## Context
29	
30	[RFC-0097](../rfc/0097-agent-skill-engineering.md) establishes a portable
31	agent-skill-engineering pack with a same-pack OKF corpus and an integration-only
32	reference router. It also requires optional consumers such as `work-loop` and
33	`architect-design` to obtain bounded knowledge through explicit provider
34	invocation.
35	
36	Explicit invocation does not require a consumer to hard-code a provider. The
37	repository's existing grounding workflows first detect eligible knowledge
38	surfaces: `architect-design` considers in-repository documentation and
39	preauthenticated retrieval capabilities, `work-loop` grounds load-bearing
40	domain claims when a relevant surface is available, and contract acquisition
41	can select a curated framework or platform skill. This capability-oriented
42	discovery lets an organization standards skill, framework library,
43	architecture reference, or agent-skills reference contribute grounding without
44	making its product identity part of every consumer's portable contract.
45	
46	[ADR-0093](0093-okf-reference-corpora-remain-governed-build-time-sources.md)
47	places a different boundary around OKF itself. Raw OKF remains a governed,
48	same-pack build-time source. Runtime workflows consume ordinary compiled
49	references; they do not dynamically interpret a source corpus. Today the
50	`architect` and `core` packs make this ownership explicit through declared OKF
51	bundles and generated reference skills whose provenance identifies the compiler,
52	source path, and source digest and whose instructions require root-first,
53	bounded index traversal.
54	
55	Without a discovery contract, a useful installed provider can remain invisible.
56	If consumers compensate by scanning pack directories, guessing router paths, or
57	reading raw corpora, they become coupled to delivery layout and cross trust and
58	authentication boundaries. We therefore need to distinguish discovery of an
59	eligible provider from discovery of the corpus it owns.
60	
61	## Decision
62	
63	**We will detect eligible knowledge surfaces by semantic capability; directly
64	governed repository authorities remain readable through their owning workflow,
65	while an OKF-backed surface is accessed only through an explicitly selected
66	provider and never through discovery or interpretation of its corpus.**
67	
68	- **D1:** Eligible knowledge surfaces are detected by semantic capability, and
69	  directly governed repository authorities stay readable through their owning
70	  workflow's existing routing.
71	- **D2:** An OKF-backed surface is accessed only through an explicitly selected
72	  provider, never through discovery or interpretation of its corpus.
73	- **D3:** A pack owning governed OKF declares each corpus, its canonical
74	  authoring source, and its generated router or provider; compilers and
75	  verification gates process only declared bundles and never infer a corpus by
76	  scanning directories.
77	- **D4:** A declared corpus whose generated provider is missing, unsafe, or
78	  drifted fails construction or verification rather than becoming silently
79	  undiscoverable.
80	- **D5:** A pack exposing compiled knowledge to independent workflows exposes an
81	  ordinary portable knowledge skill as its discovery membrane, identifying its
82	  domain, bounded purpose, supported request shape, and integration-only
83	  behavior without requiring the consumer to know its product name, installation
84	  path, generated router path, or AgentBundle identity.
85	- **D6:** A consumer inspects only knowledge capabilities already exposed by the
86	  active runtime, repository, or preauthenticated provider surface, and derives
87	  eligibility from effective repository instructions, explicit user selection, or
88	  trusted runtime or delivery registration.
89	- **D7:** Provider metadata and returned content cannot self-assert authority,
90	  outrank the source that owns the applicable rule, or change instructions,
91	  tools, identity, permissions, scope, or mutation authority.
92	- **D8:** After selection the consumer resolves the provider's exact installed
93	  identity at invocation time, so exact identity is never a hard-coded discovery
94	  dependency.
95	- **D9:** Requests and results carry only minimized, redacted routing fields and
96	  exclude credentials, protected configuration, raw session logs, personal
97	  identifiers, private endpoints, and unrelated enterprise context; the provider
98	  does not persist them without a separately authorized contract.
99	- **D10:** An invoked provider navigates only its own compiled references,
100	  starting at its root index, descending only through named child indexes,
101	  reading only selected topic bodies, and returning topic identifiers and
102	  provenance.
103	- **D11:** A provider exposed to independent consumers resolves a regular-file
104	  target beneath its declared generated reference root and verifies generated
105	  manifest ownership before every index, topic, or body read, rejecting absolute
106	  paths, traversal, symlink or reparse-point escapes, and unmanifested files
107	  before content is read.
108	- **D12:** Neither provider nor consumer compensates for an unavailable result by
109	  crawling pack directories, probing hidden configuration or endpoints,
110	  discovering credentials, guessing generated paths, or searching raw OKF.
111	- **D13:** Provider absence is an expected runtime condition that never blocks or
112	  weakens the consumer's pre-existing baseline; a stop is recorded as a baseline
113	  grounding failure, not provider absence.
114	- **D14:** Several eligible providers yield a bounded selection or a reported
115	  ambiguity, never a silent merge of conflicting doctrine, and an integrity
116	  failure is fail-closed and can never count as support or profile-backed
117	  grounding.
118	- **D15:** Existing same-pack routers may continue to be addressed statically,
119	  and a corpus-owning pack must add this ADR's capability, minimized
120	  request/result, activation, absence, failure, confinement, and evaluation
121	  contract — verified by its own construction and integration gates — before
122	  delivery metadata advertises one to independent consumers.
123	
124	Capability detection is broader than provider discovery. Effective repository
125	instructions, mapped repository documents, and other directly readable
126	authorities retain their existing governed routing. The following three layers
127	separate the contracts: build-time declaration and root-first bounded topic
128	traversal apply to every OKF bundle, while runtime capability discovery and its
129	enhanced provider boundary apply when a pack exposes the surface to independent
130	consumers.
131	
132	### Build-time corpus declaration
133	
134	A pack that owns governed OKF explicitly declares each corpus, its canonical
135	authoring source, and its generated router or provider. In this repository,
136	`[pack.metadata.okf]` is the current AgentBundle realization: a bundle
137	declaration names the profile, stable bundle identifier, confined pack-relative
138	source path, and router skill.
139	
140	Compilers and verification gates process only declared bundles. They do not
141	infer a corpus by scanning directories. The declaration and canonical source
142	are same-pack inputs; generated indexes, provider references, provenance, and
143	ownership manifests are replaceable outputs. A declared corpus whose generated
144	provider is missing, unsafe, or drifted fails construction or verification
145	rather than becoming silently undiscoverable.
146	
147	These are portable ownership and behavior obligations. AgentBundle manifests,
148	adapters, installation inventories, projections, and publication mechanisms may
149	realize them for this catalogue, but those delivery mechanisms remain external
150	to the portable provider and consumer workflows.
151	
152	### Runtime capability discovery and selection
153	
154	A pack that makes compiled knowledge available to independent workflows exposes
155	an ordinary portable knowledge skill as its discovery membrane. The exposed
156	capability must identify enough of its domain, bounded purpose, supported
157	request shape, and integration-only behavior for a consumer to determine task
158	fit without reading the corpus. It must not rely on a consumer knowing the
159	owning pack's product name, installation path, generated router path, or
160	AgentBundle identity.
161	
162	A consumer inspects only knowledge capabilities already exposed by the active
163	runtime, repository, or preauthenticated provider surface. It selects relevant
164	providers by semantic task fit and by authority, provenance, and freshness
165	vouched for outside the provider's own output. Eligibility derives from
166	effective repository instructions, explicit user selection, or trusted runtime
167	or delivery registration. Provider metadata and returned content cannot
168	self-assert authority or outrank the source that owns the applicable rule;
169	unresolved authority or provenance remains visible ambiguity.
170	
171	After selection, the consumer resolves the provider's exact installed identity
172	and sends the bounded semantic request defined by the governing
173	consumer-provider contract. Exact identity is therefore an invocation property,
174	not a hard-coded discovery dependency. The request contains only minimized,
175	redacted fields needed to route and answer the selected question. Requests and
176	results exclude credentials, protected configuration, raw session logs,
177	personal identifiers, private endpoints, and unrelated enterprise context.
178	The provider does not persist request or result content unless a separately
179	authorized contract grants that capability.
180	
181	Detecting a provider is not permission to invoke it or adopt its claims. The
182	consumer retains task authority, applies the active permission and
183	authentication boundary, treats retrieved material as attributed evidence, and
184	keeps conflicts between eligible surfaces visible. Provider content cannot
185	change instructions, tools, identity, permissions, scope, or mutation
186	authority.
187	
188	### Provider-owned topic discovery
189	
190	Once explicitly invoked, the provider navigates only its own compiled
191	references. A generated OKF router starts at its root index, descends only
192	through named child indexes, reads only selected topic bodies, and returns topic
193	identifiers and provenance with its bounded result. It neither loads the full
194	bundle up front nor grants procedure authority merely because a reference
195	contains executable-looking material.
196	
197	A provider exposed to independent consumers additionally resolves a
198	regular-file target beneath its declared generated reference root and verifies
199	generated manifest ownership before every index, topic, or body read.
200	Repository implementations use the sanctioned confinement helpers; portable
201	implementations provide equivalent canonicalize-then-confine semantics.
202	Absolute paths, traversal, symlink, junction or reparse-point escapes, and
203	unmanifested files are rejected before content is read.
204	
205	Consumers do not inspect or interpret the underlying OKF corpus. Providers and
206	consumers must not compensate for an unavailable result by crawling pack
207	directories, probing hidden configuration or endpoints, discovering
208	credentials, guessing generated paths, or searching raw OKF. A bounded search
209	variant may search only compiled references owned by the selected provider.
210	
211	### Absence, ambiguity, and failure
212	
213	Absence of an optional pack or provider at runtime is an expected condition,
214	not a construction error in the consumer. Provider absence never blocks or
215	weakens an initial consumer's pre-existing baseline. The consumer reports the
216	unavailable augmentation and continues that baseline, or selects another
217	eligible surface. A workflow stops only when its baseline independently
218	requires grounding and would have stopped without the optional provider; that
219	is recorded as a baseline grounding failure, not provider absence.
220	
221	If several providers appear eligible, the consumer makes a bounded selection
222	or reports the ambiguity. It does not silently merge conflicting doctrine. If
223	a detected provider is malformed, unavailable, or refuses the request, it
224	returns or produces a stable, redacted failure and the consumer applies the
225	same baseline rule. Discovery and invocation attempts are bounded; diagnostics
226	do not disclose sensitive paths, endpoints, credential names, or request
227	content. An integrity failure is fail-closed: it cannot count as support or
228	profile-backed grounding, although the consumer may select a different,
229	independently eligible provider. Presence or failure never creates permission
230	for raw corpus discovery.
231	
232	### Existing same-pack routers
233	
234	The current `architecture-lenses-reference` and
235	`security-checklists-reference` skills are build-time declaration,
236	provenance, and bounded-traversal precedents. Their authored same-pack consumers
237	may continue to address them statically because source, provider, and consumer
238	share one pack ownership and delivery boundary.
239	
240	Those generated routers are not thereby advertised as optional providers for
241	independent consumers. Before a corpus-owning pack exposes one that way, that
242	pack's owner adds the capability, minimized request and result, activation,
243	absence, failure, confinement, and evaluation contract required by this ADR.
244	The owning pack's construction and integration gates verify the upgrade before
245	delivery metadata advertises it. This ADR creates no standalone migration of
246	existing same-pack consumers; the agent-skill-engineering foundation is the
247	first required cross-pack realization because RFC-0097 already assigns it
248	independent consumers.
249	
250	## Decision drivers
251	
252	- Use available enterprise, repository, framework, architecture, and
253	  agent-skills knowledge for domain grounding.
254	- Keep consumers portable and independent of another pack's product identity
255	  and filesystem layout.
256	- Preserve ADR-0093's governed build-time source and same-pack ownership rule.
257	- Make discovery, selection, routing, provenance, absence, and conflict
258	  behavior deterministic enough to evaluate independently.
259	- Preserve authentication isolation, least authority, and the
260	  instruction-versus-data boundary.
261	- Keep AgentBundle-specific delivery outside the portable skill contract.
262	
263	## Consequences
264	
265	**Positive:**
266	
267	- Installed knowledge can improve a workflow without becoming a mandatory or
268	  hard-coded dependency.
269	- Packs have a clear obligation to make an intended knowledge surface visible
270	  through a bounded provider before advertising it to independent consumers,
271	  rather than merely shipping a hidden corpus.
272	- Consumers discover a capability, while providers retain corpus ownership,
273	  progressive routing, provenance, and lifecycle semantics.
274	- Missing optional providers degrade predictably, and invalid declared
275	  providers fail at the owning construction boundary.
276	- Authentication and mutation authority remain with the runtime and consuming
277	  workflow rather than flowing from retrieved content.
278	
279	**Negative:**
280	
281	- Provider owners must maintain capability descriptions, compiled routers,
282	  provenance, negative activation behavior, data minimization, confinement,
283	  and absence/failure fixtures.
284	- Consumers need explicit selection and conflict behavior instead of a single
285	  assumed provider name.
286	- Runtimes with weak skill enumeration or explicit-only activation support may
287	  require external adapter metadata while retaining the same portable
288	  semantics.
289	- Capability metadata can drift from the compiled corpus unless construction
290	  and router-precision gates verify them together.
291	
292	**Revisit if:** portable skill runtimes adopt a standard, security-preserving
293	provider-capability negotiation protocol that subsumes this contract.
294	
295	## Confirmation
296	
297	- **Mode:** architecture fitness test
298	- **Signal:** Fixtures prove declared-corpus-to-provider completeness;
299	  capability-based discovery followed by exact-identity invocation; root-first
300	  bounded topic traversal with provenance for every generated router; and, for
301	  independently exposed providers, per-read confinement with manifest
302	  ownership, externally anchored eligibility, minimized non-persistent requests
303	  and results, clean absence that preserves the consumer baseline, bounded
304	  redacted failures, fail-closed malformed or drifted providers, visible
305	  ambiguity and conflict, negative activation, and no independent-consumer
306	  access to catalogue source-pack, installation, generated-router, raw-OKF,
307	  hidden-configuration, endpoint, or credential paths. The fixture set includes
308	  organization standards, framework-library, architecture-reference, and
309	  agent-skills-reference surfaces. Separate same-pack static-router fixtures
310	  prove root-first access stays within the router's own generated reference root
311	  without imposing the independent-consumer discovery membrane.
312	- **Owner:** catalogue and corpus-owning pack maintainers
313	
314	## Alternatives considered
315	
316	- **Hard-code provider identities in every consumer** — rejected against *keep
317	  consumers portable and independent of another pack's product identity and
318	  filesystem layout*: it makes portable workflows depend on another pack's
319	  product name and installed layout, prevents equivalent organization or
320	  framework providers from participating, and confuses exact invocation with
321	  discovery.
322	- **Forbid cross-pack discovery and use only same-pack knowledge** — rejected
323	  against *use available enterprise, repository, framework, architecture, and
324	  agent-skills knowledge for domain grounding*: it leaves available domain
325	  grounding unused and forces consumers to duplicate doctrine or operate with
326	  avoidably low confidence.
327	- **Discover corpora by filesystem convention or raw OKF search** — rejected
328	  against *preserve ADR-0093's governed build-time source and same-pack ownership
329	  rule*: it violates ADR-0093, couples consumers to authoring and delivery
330	  layout, bypasses provider routing and provenance, and broadens filesystem and
331	  instruction-injection exposure.
332	- **Centralize all knowledge in one shared runtime service** — rejected against
333	  *preserve authentication isolation, least authority, and the
334	  instruction-versus-data boundary*: it moves corpus ownership, availability,
335	  authentication, and version compatibility into a mandatory service boundary,
336	  though the provider-mediated contract permits such a service when exposed as an
337	  eligible capability.
338	- **Copy relevant corpus material into each consumer pack** — rejected against
339	  *preserve ADR-0093's governed build-time source and same-pack ownership rule*:
340	  it creates competing authorities and synchronization work, and the repository
341	  already has evidence that copied taxonomies require parity tooling and drift.
342	- **Use only delivery-time integration declarations** — rejected against *keep
343	  AgentBundle-specific delivery outside the portable skill contract*: external
344	  declarations such as `pack.integrations` can describe installed composition and
345	  fallback without polluting portable instructions, but they do not let a
346	  workflow recognize other already-authorized organization, repository,
347	  framework, architecture, or agent-skills knowledge surfaces by capability.
348	
349	## References
350	
351	- [RFC-0097: Agent Skill Engineering](../rfc/0097-agent-skill-engineering.md)
352	- [ADR-0093: OKF reference corpora remain governed build-time sources within
353	  their owning pack](0093-okf-reference-corpora-remain-governed-build-time-sources.md)
354	- [`architect` OKF bundle declaration](../../packs/architect/pack.toml)
355	- [`architecture-lenses-reference` generated provider](../../packs/architect/.apm/skills/architecture-lenses-reference/SKILL.md)
356	- [`security-checklists-reference` generated provider](../../packs/core/.apm/skills/security-checklists-reference/SKILL.md)

credentials, guessing generated paths, or searching raw OKF. A bounded search
variant may search only compiled references owned by the selected provider.

### Absence, ambiguity, and failure

Absence of an optional pack or provider at runtime is an expected condition,
not a construction error in the consumer. Provider absence never blocks or
weakens an initial consumer's pre-existing baseline. The consumer reports the
unavailable augmentation and continues that baseline, or selects another
eligible surface. A workflow stops only when its baseline independently
requires grounding and would have stopped without the optional provider; that
is recorded as a baseline grounding failure, not provider absence.

If several providers appear eligible, the consumer makes a bounded selection
or reports the ambiguity. It does not silently merge conflicting doctrine. If
a detected provider is malformed, unavailable, or refuses the request, it
returns or produces a stable, redacted failure and the consumer applies the
same baseline rule. Discovery and invocation attempts are bounded; diagnostics
do not disclose sensitive paths, endpoints, credential names, or request
content. An integrity failure is fail-closed: it cannot count as support or
profile-backed grounding, although the consumer may select a different,
independently eligible provider. Presence or failure never creates permission
for raw corpus discovery.

### Existing same-pack routers

The current `architecture-lenses-reference` and
`security-checklists-reference` skills are build-time declaration,
provenance, and bounded-traversal precedents. Their authored same-pack consumers
may continue to address them statically because source, provider, and consumer
share one pack ownership and delivery boundary.

Those generated routers are not thereby advertised as optional providers for
independent consumers. Before a corpus-owning pack exposes one that way, that
pack's owner adds the capability, minimized request and result, activation,
absence, failure, confinement, and evaluation contract required by this ADR.
The owning pack's construction and integration gates verify the upgrade before
delivery metadata advertises it. This ADR creates no standalone migration of
existing same-pack consumers; the agent-skill-engineering foundation is the
first required cross-pack realization because RFC-0097 already assigns it
independent consumers.

## Decision drivers

- Use available enterprise, repository, framework, architecture, and
  agent-skills knowledge for domain grounding.
- Keep consumers portable and independent of another pack's product identity
  and filesystem layout.
- Preserve ADR-0093's governed build-time source and same-pack ownership rule.
- Make discovery, selection, routing, provenance, absence, and conflict
  behavior deterministic enough to evaluate independently.
- Preserve authentication isolation, least authority, and the
  instruction-versus-data boundary.
- Keep AgentBundle-specific delivery outside the portable skill contract.

## Consequences

**Positive:**

- Installed knowledge can improve a workflow without becoming a mandatory or
  hard-coded dependency.
- Packs have a clear obligation to make an intended knowledge surface visible
  through a bounded provider before advertising it to independent consumers,
  rather than merely shipping a hidden corpus.
- Consumers discover a capability, while providers retain corpus ownership,
  progressive routing, provenance, and lifecycle semantics.
- Missing optional providers degrade predictably, and invalid declared
  providers fail at the owning construction boundary.
- Authentication and mutation authority remain with the runtime and consuming
  workflow rather than flowing from retrieved content.

**Negative:**

- Provider owners must maintain capability descriptions, compiled routers,
  provenance, negative activation behavior, data minimization, confinement,
  and absence/failure fixtures.
- Consumers need explicit selection and conflict behavior instead of a single
  assumed provider name.
- Runtimes with weak skill enumeration or explicit-only activation support may
  require external adapter metadata while retaining the same portable
  semantics.
- Capability metadata can drift from the compiled corpus unless construction
  and router-precision gates verify them together.

**Revisit if:** portable skill runtimes adopt a standard, security-preserving
provider-capability negotiation protocol that subsumes this contract.

## Confirmation

- **Mode:** architecture fitness test
- **Signal:** Fixtures prove declared-corpus-to-provider completeness;
  capability-based discovery followed by exact-identity invocation; root-first
  bounded topic traversal with provenance for every generated router; and, for
  independently exposed providers, per-read confinement with manifest
  ownership, externally anchored eligibility, minimized non-persistent requests
  and results, clean absence that preserves the consumer baseline, bounded
  redacted failures, fail-closed malformed or drifted providers, visible
  ambiguity and conflict, negative activation, and no independent-consumer
  access to catalogue source-pack, installation, generated-router, raw-OKF,
  hidden-configuration, endpoint, or credential paths. The fixture set includes
  organization standards, framework-library, architecture-reference, and
  agent-skills-reference surfaces. Separate same-pack static-router fixtures
  prove root-first access stays within the router's own generated reference root
  without imposing the independent-consumer discovery membrane.
- **Owner:** catalogue and corpus-owning pack maintainers

## Alternatives considered

- **Hard-code provider identities in every consumer** — rejected against *keep
  consumers portable and independent of another pack's product identity and
  filesystem layout*: it makes portable workflows depend on another pack's
  product name and installed layout, prevents equivalent organization or
  framework providers from participating, and confuses exact invocation with
  discovery.
- **Forbid cross-pack discovery and use only same-pack knowledge** — rejected
  against *use available enterprise, repository, framework, architecture, and
  agent-skills knowledge for domain grounding*: it leaves available domain
  grounding unused and forces consumers to duplicate doctrine or operate with
  avoidably low confidence.
- **Discover corpora by filesystem convention or raw OKF search** — rejected
  against *preserve ADR-0093's governed build-time source and same-pack ownership
  rule*: it violates ADR-0093, couples consumers to authoring and delivery
  layout, bypasses provider routing and provenance, and broadens filesystem and
  instruction-injection exposure.
- **Centralize all knowledge in one shared runtime service** — rejected against
  *preserve authentication isolation, least authority, and the
  instruction-versus-data boundary*: it moves corpus ownership, availability,
  authentication, and version compatibility into a mandatory service boundary,
  though the provider-mediated contract permits such a service when exposed as an
  eligible capability.
- **Copy relevant corpus material into each consumer pack** — rejected against
  *preserve ADR-0093's governed build-time source and same-pack ownership rule*:
  it creates competing authorities and synchronization work, and the repository
  already has evidence that copied taxonomies require parity tooling and drift.
- **Use only delivery-time integration declarations** — rejected against *keep
  AgentBundle-specific delivery outside the portable skill contract*: external
  declarations such as `pack.integrations` can describe installed composition and
  fallback without polluting portable instructions, but they do not let a
  workflow recognize other already-authorized organization, repository,
  framework, architecture, or agent-skills knowledge surfaces by capability.

## References

- [RFC-0097: Agent Skill Engineering](../rfc/0097-agent-skill-engineering.md)
- [ADR-0093: OKF reference corpora remain governed build-time sources within
  their owning pack](0093-okf-reference-corpora-remain-governed-build-time-sources.md)
- [`architect` OKF bundle declaration](../../packs/architect/pack.toml)
- [`architecture-lenses-reference` generated provider](../../packs/architect/.apm/skills/architecture-lenses-reference/SKILL.md)
- [`security-checklists-reference` generated provider](../../packs/core/.apm/skills/security-checklists-reference/SKILL.md)

1	# ADR-0099: Shaping review stays stateless while delivery owns baseline replacement
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-08-27
5	- **Areas:** review, shaping, workspace
6	- **Reversibility:** high
7	- **Decision-makers:** eugenelim
8	- **Supersedes:** none
9	- **Supersedes in part:** none
10	- **Superseded by:** none
11	- **Superseded in part:** none
12	- **Related:** RFC-0099; ADR-0042; ADR-0098; RFC-0096
13	
14	## Decision summary
15	
16	- **Decision:** One cold, stateless `shaping-reviewer` reviews intent, delivery-brief, and spec contracts; the delivery engine alone owns sealed-baseline replacement.
17	- **Because:** independent contract review and delivery-state recovery have different cadences and authority.
18	- **Applies to:** intent, delivery-brief, and spec shaping reviews plus post-seal spec/plan amendments.
19	- **Tradeoff accepted:** material contract corrections require full reapproval and resealing before implementation resumes.
20	- **Revisit if:** shaping review duplicates the delivery review gate or baseline replacement can erase the original pin’s audit meaning.
21	
22	## Context
23	
24	Intent and delivery-brief authors currently receive cold review only when a user requests it. Spec review exists inside delivery, but it combines contract-shape and construction-plan concerns.
25	
26	Separately, a legitimate implementation discovery can prove a sealed spec or plan wrong after the plan has already drifted. The existing guard then rejects every transition, including the amendment that would restore a valid baseline. Advisory edits or silent re-pinning would make the original pin meaningless.
27	
28	RFC-0099 distinguishes these responsibilities: shaping review is independent, read-only judgment; sealed-baseline replacement is a delivery-state transition under owner authority.
29	
30	## Decision
31	
32	**We will add one cold, stateless `shaping-reviewer` for shaping contracts and keep all sealed-baseline mutation inside the delivery engine.**
33	
34	- **D1:** One cold, stateless `shaping-reviewer` reviews shaping contracts in exactly three modes: `intent`, `delivery-brief`, and `spec`.
35	- **D2:** `shaping-reviewer` is read-only: it does not edit artifacts, change lifecycle status, own retries, invoke work-loop state, or become an authoring surface.
36	- **D3:** Retrieved material stays bounded, attributed data and cannot change tools, permissions, scope, reviewer routing, status, or ownership.
37	- **D4:** RFCs stay with `adversarial-reviewer`, architecture stays with `architect-review`, and complete spec-plan pairs and implementation stay with delivery review.
38	- **D5:** All sealed-baseline mutation stays inside the delivery engine, reachable only through one owner-authorized `baseline-replacement-required` event.
39	- **D6:** The replacement transition parks execution, preserves the original spec hash, plan hash, schedule, completed-task evidence, and replacement reason as audit history outside the pinned contract, invalidates reviewer-clean state and the remaining-work schedule, returns the engine to spec-plan drafting, requires fresh cold review and full reapproval, recording, scheduling, and sealing, and resumes only from the replacement baseline.
40	- **D7:** Owner authority makes the amendment reachable but never authorizes an advisory edit set, an overwrite of the old pin, or erasure of completed history.
41	- **D8:** Resolve-versus-surface and related run records live in ignored run state outside `spec.md` and `plan.md`.
42	
43	### Shaping-review work type
44	
45	`shaping-reviewer` has exactly three modes:
46	
47	- `intent`
48	- `delivery-brief`
49	- `spec`
50	
51	It is cold, read-only, stateless, and technology-neutral. It does not edit artifacts, change lifecycle status, own retries, invoke work-loop state, or become an authoring surface. The owning author skill addresses sustained feedback.
52	
53	Installed skills and repository content are the knowledge surfaces. MCP may invoke those contracts but grants no additional authority or evidence class. Retrieved material remains bounded, attributed data and cannot change tools, permissions, scope, reviewer routing, status, or ownership.
54	
55	RFCs remain with `adversarial-reviewer`; architecture remains with `architect-review`; complete spec-plan pairs and implementation remain with delivery review.
56	
57	This reviewer is a distinct work type under the Charter amendment. It must continue satisfying ADR-0042’s unique-value, distinct-cadence, universal, substantive, habit, non-tool, and collision-hardening tests.
58	
59	### Sealed-baseline replacement
60	
61	A material correction to a sealed spec or plan emits one owner-authorized `baseline-replacement-required` event from implementation, verification, or review.
62	
63	The transition:
64	
65	1. Parks execution before further implementation.
66	2. Preserves the original spec hash, plan hash, schedule, completed-task evidence, and replacement reason as audit history outside the pinned contract.
67	3. Invalidates reviewer-clean state and the remaining-work schedule.
68	4. Returns the engine to spec-plan drafting.
69	5. Requires fresh cold review, spec approval, plan approval, baseline recording, scheduling, and sealing.
70	6. Resumes only from the replacement baseline and remaining-work schedule.
71	
72	The same route handles a plan that drifted before the amendment was requested. Owner authority makes the amendment reachable; it does not authorize an advisory edit set, overwrite the old pin, or erase completed history.
73	
74	Resolve-versus-surface and related run records live in ignored run state outside `spec.md` and `plan.md`. They are operational records, not additions to the pinned contract.
75	
76	## Decision drivers
77	
78	- Give intent and brief contracts independent review without overloading work-loop.
79	- Preserve one owner per review cadence.
80	- Keep shaping review usable without a state engine.
81	- Make recovery reachable after legitimate drift.
82	- Preserve the original baseline as audit evidence.
83	- Require explicit owner authority and full reapproval for material amendments.
84	
85	## Consequences
86	
87	**Positive:**
88	
89	- Intent, delivery-brief, and spec contracts receive repeatable cold review.
90	- Review findings return to the correct lifecycle owner.
91	- A drifted plan has one guarded recovery path instead of permanent deadlock.
92	- Original and replacement baselines remain distinguishable.
93	- Completed work evidence survives re-planning.
94	
95	**Negative:**
96	
97	- The catalogue gains one reviewer agent.
98	- Material amendments incur another complete approval and review sequence.
99	- The delivery engine must carry crash recovery and audit evidence for replacement mutations.
100	- Shaping and delivery reviewers need fixtures preventing judgment overlap.
101	
102	**Revisit if:** shaping review duplicates the delivery review gate or baseline replacement can erase the original pin’s audit meaning.
103	
104	## Confirmation
105	
106	- **Mode:** architecture fitness test
107	- **Signal:** reviewer-collision fixtures prove distinct cadence and judgment; delivery-state tests prove guarded entry from every code phase, lossless invalidation, crash recovery, full resealing, and refusal of stale baseline resumption.
108	- **Owner:** Core maintainers
109	
110	## Alternatives considered
111	
112	- **Keep shaping review ad hoc** — rejected against *give intent and brief contracts independent review without overloading work-loop*: authors can remain their own only reviewer.
113	- **Extend `adversarial-reviewer` to all shaping artifacts** — rejected against *preserve one owner per review cadence*: it overloads the code/spec-plan reviewer and collapses distinct cadences.
114	- **Add a stateful shaping loop or reuse work-loop scripts** — rejected against *keep shaping review usable without a state engine*: shaping review needs no engine, retries, or delivery state.
115	- **Allow bounded advisory plan edits** — rejected against *require explicit owner authority and full reapproval for material amendments*: an advisory path weakens the pin and cannot safely recover an already-drifted plan.
116	- **Replace the stored hash in place** — rejected against *preserve the original baseline as audit evidence*: it destroys the evidence that the approved baseline changed.
117	
118	## References
119	
120	- RFC-0099: Cut before adding and artifact shaping.
121	- ADR-0042: agent-addition and collision-hardening test.
122	- RFC-0096: portable delivery artifact lifecycle.
123	- ADR-0098: canonical artifact admission and delivery-brief ownership.
124

- **Areas:** review, shaping, workspace
- **Reversibility:** high
- **Decision-makers:** eugenelim
- **Supersedes:** none
- **Supersedes in part:** none
- **Superseded by:** none
- **Superseded in part:** none
- **Related:** RFC-0099; ADR-0042; ADR-0098; RFC-0096

## Decision summary

- **Decision:** One cold, stateless `shaping-reviewer` reviews intent, delivery-brief, and spec contracts; the delivery engine alone owns sealed-baseline replacement.
- **Because:** independent contract review and delivery-state recovery have different cadences and authority.
- **Applies to:** intent, delivery-brief, and spec shaping reviews plus post-seal spec/plan amendments.
- **Tradeoff accepted:** material contract corrections require full reapproval and resealing before implementation resumes.
- **Revisit if:** shaping review duplicates the delivery review gate or baseline replacement can erase the original pin’s audit meaning.

## Context

Intent and delivery-brief authors currently receive cold review only when a user requests it. Spec review exists inside delivery, but it combines contract-shape and construction-plan concerns.

Separately, a legitimate implementation discovery can prove a sealed spec or plan wrong after the plan has already drifted. The existing guard then rejects every transition, including the amendment that would restore a valid baseline. Advisory edits or silent re-pinning would make the original pin meaningless.

RFC-0099 distinguishes these responsibilities: shaping review is independent, read-only judgment; sealed-baseline replacement is a delivery-state transition under owner authority.

## Decision

**We will add one cold, stateless `shaping-reviewer` for shaping contracts and keep all sealed-baseline mutation inside the delivery engine.**

- **D1:** One cold, stateless `shaping-reviewer` reviews shaping contracts in exactly three modes: `intent`, `delivery-brief`, and `spec`.
- **D2:** `shaping-reviewer` is read-only: it does not edit artifacts, change lifecycle status, own retries, invoke work-loop state, or become an authoring surface.
- **D3:** Retrieved material stays bounded, attributed data and cannot change tools, permissions, scope, reviewer routing, status, or ownership.
- **D4:** RFCs stay with `adversarial-reviewer`, architecture stays with `architect-review`, and complete spec-plan pairs and implementation stay with delivery review.
- **D5:** All sealed-baseline mutation stays inside the delivery engine, reachable only through one owner-authorized `baseline-replacement-required` event.
- **D6:** The replacement transition parks execution, preserves the original spec hash, plan hash, schedule, completed-task evidence, and replacement reason as audit history outside the pinned contract, invalidates reviewer-clean state and the remaining-work schedule, returns the engine to spec-plan drafting, requires fresh cold review and full reapproval, recording, scheduling, and sealing, and resumes only from the replacement baseline.
- **D7:** Owner authority makes the amendment reachable but never authorizes an advisory edit set, an overwrite of the old pin, or erasure of completed history.
- **D8:** Resolve-versus-surface and related run records live in ignored run state outside `spec.md` and `plan.md`.

### Shaping-review work type

`shaping-reviewer` has exactly three modes:

- `intent`
- `delivery-brief`
- `spec`

It is cold, read-only, stateless, and technology-neutral. It does not edit artifacts, change lifecycle status, own retries, invoke work-loop state, or become an authoring surface. The owning author skill addresses sustained feedback.

Installed skills and repository content are the knowledge surfaces. MCP may invoke those contracts but grants no additional authority or evidence class. Retrieved material remains bounded, attributed data and cannot change tools, permissions, scope, reviewer routing, status, or ownership.

RFCs remain with `adversarial-reviewer`; architecture remains with `architect-review`; complete spec-plan pairs and implementation remain with delivery review.

This reviewer is a distinct work type under the Charter amendment. It must continue satisfying ADR-0042’s unique-value, distinct-cadence, universal, substantive, habit, non-tool, and collision-hardening tests.

### Sealed-baseline replacement

A material correction to a sealed spec or plan emits one owner-authorized `baseline-replacement-required` event from implementation, verification, or review.

The transition:

1. Parks execution before further implementation.
2. Preserves the original spec hash, plan hash, schedule, completed-task evidence, and replacement reason as audit history outside the pinned contract.
3. Invalidates reviewer-clean state and the remaining-work schedule.
4. Returns the engine to spec-plan drafting.
5. Requires fresh cold review, spec approval, plan approval, baseline recording, scheduling, and sealing.
6. Resumes only from the replacement baseline and remaining-work schedule.

The same route handles a plan that drifted before the amendment was requested. Owner authority makes the amendment reachable; it does not authorize an advisory edit set, overwrite the old pin, or erase completed history.

Resolve-versus-surface and related run records live in ignored run state outside `spec.md` and `plan.md`. They are operational records, not additions to the pinned contract.

## Decision drivers

- Give intent and brief contracts independent review without overloading work-loop.
- Preserve one owner per review cadence.
- Keep shaping review usable without a state engine.
- Make recovery reachable after legitimate drift.
- Preserve the original baseline as audit evidence.
- Require explicit owner authority and full reapproval for material amendments.

## Consequences

**Positive:**

- Intent, delivery-brief, and spec contracts receive repeatable cold review.
- Review findings return to the correct lifecycle owner.
- A drifted plan has one guarded recovery path instead of permanent deadlock.
- Original and replacement baselines remain distinguishable.
- Completed work evidence survives re-planning.

**Negative:**

- The catalogue gains one reviewer agent.
- Material amendments incur another complete approval and review sequence.
- The delivery engine must carry crash recovery and audit evidence for replacement mutations.
- Shaping and delivery reviewers need fixtures preventing judgment overlap.

**Revisit if:** shaping review duplicates the delivery review gate or baseline replacement can erase the original pin’s audit meaning.

## Confirmation

- **Mode:** architecture fitness test
- **Signal:** reviewer-collision fixtures prove distinct cadence and judgment; delivery-state tests prove guarded entry from every code phase, lossless invalidation, crash recovery, full resealing, and refusal of stale baseline resumption.
- **Owner:** Core maintainers

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep shaping review ad hoc** — rejected against *give intent and brief contracts independent review without overloading work-loop*: authors can remain their own only reviewer.
- **Extend `adversarial-reviewer` to all shaping artifacts** — rejected against *preserve one owner per review cadence*: it overloads the code/spec-plan reviewer and collapses distinct cadences.
- **Add a stateful shaping loop or reuse work-loop scripts** — rejected against *keep shaping review usable without a state engine*: shaping review needs no engine, retries, or delivery state.
- **Allow bounded advisory plan edits** — rejected against *require explicit owner authority and full reapproval for material amendments*: an advisory path weakens the pin and cannot safely recover an already-drifted plan.
- **Replace the stored hash in place** — rejected against *preserve the original baseline as audit evidence*: it destroys the evidence that the approved baseline changed.

## References

- RFC-0099: Cut before adding and artifact shaping.
- ADR-0042: agent-addition and collision-hardening test.
- RFC-0096: portable delivery artifact lifecycle.
- ADR-0098: canonical artifact admission and delivery-brief ownership.

28	
29	The durable limit is **admissible, not safe**: deterministic checks establish a bounded structural and provenance contract but never prove skill prose or scripts harmless. State-schema and manifest-schema versions are independent namespaces.
30	
31	## Decision
32	
33	> Direct sources classify after resolution, normalize into the canonical pack pipeline, and preserve pack-keyed lifecycle semantics with explicit direct provenance.
34	
35	- **D1:** A source is classified only after the resolver returns a confined
36	  directory.
37	- **D2:** A source is a catalogue only when both `catalogue.toml` and `packs/`
38	  exist; a `catalogue.toml` without `packs/` is a partial catalogue marker and
39	  refuses.
40	- **D3:** Root `SKILL.md + skills/`, root `pack.toml + SKILL.md`, unsupported
41	  nested roots, and other shape overlaps refuse; collection and direct-pack child
42	  names must equal frontmatter names, while root-single frontmatter is
43	  authoritative.
44	- **D4:** `direct_source.admit_and_normalize`, or its final explicitly named
45	  equivalent, is the single entry point through which both `validate` and install
46	  preflight reach direct classification, enforced by an import-boundary
47	  construction test; canonical `pack.toml + .apm/` paths keep their existing
48	  route.
49	- **D5:** Normalization copies into a temporary canonical pack only the byte
50	  string returned by the single confined read of each admitted regular file,
51	  never symlinks or reopened source content, and the temporary path is never
52	  provenance or receipt content.
53	- **D6:** Family-2 inventory is single-traversal, and
54	  `catalogue_tooling/file_safety.py` raises `BoundExceeded` — an
55	  `UnsafeContentError` subclass carrying the breached budget — so direct
56	  admission maps a bound to its registered diagnostic without message parsing.
57	- **D7:** A direct pack is one named, versioned, indivisible lifecycle, and a
58	  manifestless selected skill becomes one synthetic pack whose identity is its
59	  validated skill name, with the internal sentinel never rendered, compared, or
60	  publisher-claimable.
61	- **D8:** A same-name direct/other source collision at one adapter refuses in
62	  either direction; recovery is removal or rename/re-source followed by a normal
63	  install, never `--force`.
64	- **D9:** State stays keyed by `(pack name, adapter)`, direct identity is
65	  `(source-kind, canonical source, source-path)`, and digest and revision are
66	  explicitly excluded from identity.
67	- **D10:** Readers accept state schema-versions 0.4 and 0.5, and every direct
68	  state mutation goes through `agentbundle.statelock.persist_state_locked` and
69	  computes `max(existing, 0.5 if it adds or updates a direct row else 0.4)`
70	  against the state re-read inside that lock, never a pre-lock snapshot.
71	- **D11:** RFC-0098 D4 as corrected by Erratum E2 is the sole normative digest
72	  algorithm owner; the digest is content-only and version-prefixed
73	  `sha256-1:<hex>`, and executable mode is reported at report time but never
74	  persisted.
75	- **D12:** A new direct `pack.toml` must declare `schema = 1`; omission fails
76	  closed, and unsupported majors fail closed.
77	- **D13:** Within a supported major, existing field meanings are not removed,
78	  repurposed, or newly required; supported majors are N and N−1 for one named
79	  release deprecation window.
80	- **D14:** Only explicit local paths and GitHub-only non-credentialed `git+https`
81	  may carry direct content; `catalogue+https` and arbitrary archives are excluded
82	  from direct classification and no direct credentials are sent.
83	- **D15:** Direct remote intake validates and encodes archive components, refuses
84	  bare or defaulted `main`, resolves an explicit ref to a full commit SHA and
85	  records it, applies the shared credential-free `git+https` acquisition resource
86	  caps, deadline, and E11-defined GitHub/codeload redirect equivalence, and
87	  applies direct-only post-extraction link and special-entry refusal.
88	
89	### 1. Classify after resolution
90	
91	After the resolver returns a confined directory, classify an existing canonical `pack.toml + .apm/` pack through its existing path; a catalogue only when both `catalogue.toml` and `packs/` exist; otherwise a direct pack, manifestless collection, or manifestless single. A `catalogue.toml` without `packs/` is a partial catalogue marker and refuses. Root `SKILL.md + skills/`, root `pack.toml + SKILL.md`, unsupported nested roots, and other overlaps refuse. RFC-0098 E13 owns root-context disposition, AC32 owns direct measured content, and AC33 owns its budgets.
92	
93	**Consequence:** Catalogue precedence is preserved while no transport gains an implicit root-shape rule. A local path already at a skill is allowed; collection/direct-pack child names must equal frontmatter names, while root-single frontmatter is authoritative.
94	
95	**Revisit trigger:** A classification fixture requires a new precedence rule or a recursive/hidden discovery exception.
96	
97	**2026-08-28 Erratum — trigger fired, decision retained.** RFC-0098 E14 admits `.claude/skills/` as a second collection root and one bounded category level below a collection root, on corpus evidence that the single-root rule refused six of thirteen legitimate sources. This is a hidden-root exception, so the trigger above fired; the decision in §1 is retained because the exception is enumerable at fixed depth rather than recursive, and because E14 adds compensating refusals — ambiguity when both roots are present, and refusal when the source root lies inside the projection target or bears catalogue markers.
98	
99	### 2. Normalize through one named entry point
100	
101	`direct_source.admit_and_normalize` (or its final explicitly named equivalent) owns classification, confined inventory, normalization, and baseline direct admission. Both `validate` and install preflight reach direct classification only through that entry point; an import-boundary construction test enforces this. Canonical `pack.toml + .apm/` paths retain their existing route.
102	
103	Normalization copies into a temporary canonical pack only the byte string returned by the single confined read of each admitted regular file, never symlinks or reopens source content. It reuses canonical validation → rendering → planning → installation → state, and the temporary path is never provenance or receipt content.
104	
105	Family-2 inventory is likewise single-traversal. `catalogue_tooling/file_safety.py` raises `BoundExceeded`, an `UnsafeContentError` subclass carrying the breached budget, so direct admission maps a bound to its registered diagnostic without message parsing; existing catalogue callers retain their `UnsafeContentError` catch behavior. A separate direct diagnostic represents a source that cannot be traversed or changes during admission, rather than misclassifying that condition as measured-path integrity.
106	
107	**Consequence:** Byte-identical projection and plan parity against hand-authored canonical fixtures is release-critical.
108	
109	**Revisit trigger:** The import-boundary test fails or parity requires a direct-only downstream branch.
110	
111	### 3. Keep lifecycle identity pack-keyed
112	
113	A direct pack is one named/versioned indivisible lifecycle. A manifestless selected skill becomes one synthetic pack whose identity is its validated skill name; the internal sentinel is never rendered, compared, or publisher-claimable. A same-name direct/other source collision at one adapter refuses in either direction; recovery is removal or rename/re-source followed by a normal install, never `--force`.
114	
115	**Consequence:** No collection object or state hierarchy is added; manifestless rows remain independently upgradable and removable.
116	
117	**Revisit trigger:** Upgrade/uninstall demonstrably requires a durable collection identity or source conflicts cannot be recovered through existing ownership semantics.
118	
119	### 4. Add direct provenance with lazy state migration
120	
121	State remains keyed by `(pack name, adapter)`. Direct identity is `(source-kind, canonical source, source-path)`; digest and revision are explicitly excluded. `source-path` is absent for a direct pack (not empty) and validated relative POSIX for a manifestless skill; every read re-establishes source root and confinement before joining.
122	
123	Readers accept 0.4/0.5. This amends the greenfield hard-refusal posture recorded at `packages/agentbundle/agentbundle/config.py` and inherited from ADR-0039, under which a reader refused every unrecognized `schema-version` and no converter existed; the amendment is narrowed to a supported-version set on read. Every direct state mutation goes through `agentbundle.statelock.persist_state_locked` and computes `max(existing, 0.5 if it adds or updates a direct row else 0.4)` against the state re-read inside that lock, never a pre-lock snapshot: catalogue-only mutations stay 0.4 when they begin there, while an existing 0.5 file is never downgraded, including after its last direct row is removed. This preserves ADR-0039’s rollback posture for unaffected users without orphaning direct provenance. Older readers refuse 0.5 through that same existing hard refusal, whose shipped text directs reinstallation rather than migration, so the migration is intentionally reversible only for states that never acquire direct rows.
124	
125	RFC-0098 D4 as corrected by Erratum E2 is the sole normative digest algorithm owner: it defines sort key, field order, and digest-version migration; the version-prefixed digest is `sha256-1:<hex>`. Digest is content-only. Executable-mode is reported in the security summary but computed at report time and never persisted; the existing `safety.write_jailed` call-site default writes installed direct payloads non-executable, so a source-side bit does not change what lands on disk.
126	
127	**Consequence:** State migration and digest vectors are compatibility evidence, without duplicated algorithm prose.
128	
129	**Revisit trigger:** A direct row cannot be represented without changing the pack/adapter key or a new digest version is proposed.
130	
131	### 5. Require explicit direct-manifest schema and bounded support
132	
133	A new direct `pack.toml` **must** declare `schema = 1`; omission fails closed. The contract schema and bundled `_data/` copy add that top-level field in byte parity; implicit v1 remains a legacy catalogue-manifest affordance only. Within a supported major, existing field meanings are not removed, repurposed, or newly required; supported majors are N and N−1 for one named release deprecation window, after which the oldest major may be removed by a documented migration. Unsupported majors fail closed.
134	
135	**Consequence:** Manifest compatibility is explicit and separate from security controls and state versioning; the contract update is release-impacting.
136	
137	**Revisit trigger:** A proposed field requires an incompatible meaning inside a major or the release policy cannot sustain the N/N−1 window.
138	
139	### 6. Harden the direct remote boundary
140	
141	Only explicit local paths and GitHub-only non-credentialed `git+https` may carry direct content. Current resolver behavior does **not** enforce this decision yet. Direct remote intake validates and encodes archive components, refuses bare/defaulted `main`, resolves an explicit ref to a full commit SHA, records it, applies the shared credential-free `git+https` acquisition resource caps, deadline, and E11-defined GitHub/codeload redirect equivalence, and applies direct-only post-extraction link and special-entry refusal. 142	
143	The shared resolver inherits numeric bounds by reference to RFC-0098/its implementation constants, not hard-coded ADR values. Catalogue symlink support remains intact.
144	
145	**Consequence:** `catalogue+https` and arbitrary archives remain excluded from direct classification, and no direct credentials are sent.
146	
147	**Revisit trigger:** A new direct carrier or redirect host is requested, or the catalogue-symlink regression fails.
148	
149	## Consequences
150	
151	**Positive:** Existing source precedence, adapter projection, ownership, and lifecycle remain the authority; direct authors get a small, explicit contract; and direct remote provenance is commit-pinned.
152	
153	**Negative:** Direct support deliberately excludes recursive discovery, private auth, arbitrary archives, non-GitHub VCS, dependencies, recipes, and non-skill primitives. Normalization copies/hashes first, and direct state makes the affected installation incompatible with old readers.
154	
155	**Revisit if:** one of the per-decision revisit triggers above fires — a
156	classification fixture needs a new precedence rule (D1–D3), the import-boundary
157	test fails or parity requires a direct-only downstream branch (D4), a direct row
158	cannot be represented without changing the pack/adapter key or a new digest
159	version is proposed (D9–D11), the release policy cannot sustain the N/N−1 window
160	(D13), or a new direct carrier or redirect host is requested (D14–D15).
161	
162	## Confirmation
163	
164	- **Mode:** construction tests, manual CLI exercise, and security evidence.
165	- **Signal:** import-boundary, shape, canonical/direct parity, state migration, digest vector, remote URL/pin/resource, diagnostic parity, lifecycle, interrupted-install, and catalogue-symlink regression tests pass; the security-checklist record is complete.
166	- **Owner:** AgentBundle maintainers and reviewers of RFC-0098 implementation work.
167	
168	## Alternatives considered
169	
170	| Option | Trade-off |
171	| --- | --- |
172	| Require every repository to become a catalogue | Reuses machinery but imposes unnecessary catalogue structure. **Rejected against:** bounded-authoring driver. |
173	| Copy selected skills directly into runtime directories | Appears small but bypasses projection, ownership, drift, and lifecycle. **Rejected against:** canonical-lifecycle driver. |
174	| Add an install-unit model and parallel state hierarchy | Makes identities uniform but rewrites mature lifecycle machinery prematurely. **Rejected against:** reversibility and smallest-change drivers. |
175	| Normalize direct shapes into existing packs | Adds a narrow adapter and provenance while retaining established owners. **Chosen against:** all decision drivers. |
176	
177	## References
178	
179	- [RFC-0098](../rfc/0098-direct-skill-repository-installation.md) — accepted direct-source contract and binding Errata.
180	- [RFC-0085](../rfc/0085-catalogue-source-identity.md) — catalogue identity after source resolution.
181	- [ADR-0036](0036-install-source-resolves-through-trusted-precedence-chain-no-repo-source-no-cwd.md) — source precedence, including its 2026-08-11 Erratum.
182	- [ADR-0039](0039-footprint-co-ownership-install-identity-and-shared-prefix-class.md) — pack/adapter identity, ownership, and pre-direct migration posture.
